item.title: Gunman fired at US consulate in Toronto, second time building was shot at this year
item.description: The second shooting at the U.S. Consulate in Toronto this year triggered an hour-long police chase, although no arrest was made as officials continue to investigate.
item.content:encoded:
A gunman fired at the U.S. Consulate in Toronto on Monday, marking the second time this year someone shot at the building, according to authorities.

A single shell casing was found at the scene, and there was damage to the building's facade.

No injuries were reported in the incident.

"The U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Canada are open and operating normally, though some routine U.S. citizen services in Toronto are being rescheduled," the consulate said in a statement.

GUNFIRE SHATTERS TORONTO LATIN STREET FESTIVAL, LEAVING AT LEAST 2 DEAD AND MULTIPLE WOUNDED

Toronto Deputy Police Chief Frank Barredo said there was a high-speed chase after the shooting that lasted an hour. However, no arrest was made and Barredo committed to continuing the search for those involved.

"We will approach this investigation with great seriousness," Barredo said at a news conference. "We will bring the people responsible for this to justice."

Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow described the shooting as a "brazen attack."

"I want to say to the person or persons responsible, we will get you," she said.

This was the second shooting targeting the U.S. Consulate this year, with the first coming on March 10, when two suspects allegedly fired multiple shots at the building before driving away in a stolen vehicle.

Sheldon Tracy-Stewart, 18, and Zara Jabbi, 19, were arrested last month and charged with multiple offenses in connection with the March shooting. The allegations have not been tested in court.

A police presence has been seen at the consulate since the first shooting.

Barredo said a patrol vehicle was outside the consulate with its lights on when the shooting happened. Two security personnel were also in the building.

Last month, police said they believed multiple shootings, including the one in March, could be tied to "multilayered" gun-for-hire networks that have also targeted Toronto synagogues.

Two popular Jewish-owned bakeries were targeted by gunfire over the weekend.

US CONSULATE IN TORONTO STRUCK BY GUNFIRE, POLICE SAY; NO INJURIES REPORTED

Barredo said police had not ruled out a connection between Monday's consulate shooting and the attacks on the bakeries. The motive for the consulate shooting remains under investigation.

"Investigators will follow the evidence to where it leads," he said.

Doug Ford, the premier of Ontario, said he was "disgusted" by the recent violence in Toronto.

"I’m totally disgusted by the shootings and vandalism that took place in Toronto over the last few days, including at two Jewish-owned businesses over the weekend and near the U.S. Consulate this morning," he said on X. "In all cases, active police investigations are underway. I expect all those responsible to be found, prosecuted and punished to the fullest extent of the law."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy’s ex-husband details ‘big spiral’ as expert says one part ‘scared me’ in mom’s murder trial
item.description: Patrick Clancy testified about his ex-wife's mental health spiral on Seroquel and her intrusive thoughts about harming their children before the killings.
item.content:encoded:
If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

Patrick Clancy, the father of three young children strangled inside their Massachusetts home, became the first witness Monday in his ex-wife’s murder trial, offering jurors a harrowing account of the mental health decline he witnessed before their deaths.

He was the first witness called in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, who faces murder charges in the deaths of the couple's three children in January 2023. Prosecutors argue she acted deliberately, while defense attorneys contend severe mental illness drove her actions.

Patrick described watching his then-wife fall into a "big spiral" after she began taking Seroquel, testifying that she lost weight, became severely depressed and began expressing suicidal thoughts.

"Awful," he said when asked how Lindsay was doing physically after starting the medication. "That was really where her big spiral started. She started to lose a lot of weight, and she became very depressed, and she was having a really hard time."

LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN

Patrick also testified that Lindsay told him she was experiencing intrusive thoughts about harming their children, although she denied having a plan and said the thoughts disturbed her.

"I never saw Lindsay harm the kids," he told jurors.

Margaret McLean, a former criminal prosecutor and trial attorney who teaches law at Boston College’s Carroll School of Management, said Patrick’s measured delivery did little to conceal the anguish of a father being forced to retrace the months preceding his children’s deaths.

"I think his demeanor on the stand is really quite clinical. He’s telling it as it is," McLean told Fox News Digital. "You can see the anguish within this man’s eyes, his facial expressions. You can tell he’s anguished up there, and it’s a horrible thing to have to relive and talk about."

McLean said Patrick appeared to be compartmentalizing his emotions as he listened carefully to the questions and provided straightforward answers.

"He’s got to get through this," she said. "He’s got to listen to the questions and provide the answers as best he can, and I think that he’s doing that."

HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL

Patrick testified that he was not concerned for the children’s safety when Lindsay first shared that the intrusive thoughts were telling her to hurt herself as well as her children. Moments after discussing the thoughts, he said, she could be seen making the children lunch, playing with them or preparing them for bed.

Patrick told jurors that he became alarmed after Lindsay was prescribed 13 psychiatric medications in the months prior to the murders and that he pushed for an in-person appointment because he believed there was a "disconnect" between the seriousness of her condition and the brief telehealth sessions she was receiving.

"It seemed like most of her telehealth appointments were pretty quick, and there just wasn’t, like, a lot of attention," he said.

Patrick also described taking Lindsay to hospital emergency departments and helping her enter McLean Hospital after she continued expressing suicidal thoughts.

He testified that he "would have paid anything" if insurance had become an obstacle to keeping her hospitalized.

The testimony could leave jurors asking whether the warning prompted an adequate response, McLean said, while cautioning against placing blame on Patrick or family members who may not have understood the severity of the risk.

"So many people don’t understand mental health today, so I’m not blaming him at all," McLean said. "Anybody might have done what he did, but that’s the part that scared me."

WATCH: Lindsay Clancy clutches tissues as jurors hear about her three children

GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL

Patrick’s testimony followed starkly different opening statements from prosecutors and the defense.

Assistant District Attorney Shanan Buckingham told jurors that Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, were "deliberately and meticulously killed" by their mother on Jan. 24, 2023.

Buckingham alleged that Clancy deliberately sent Patrick from their Duxbury home to pick up medication and takeout food, giving herself enough time to strangle each child with an exercise band before attempting to kill herself.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

McLean said Buckingham gave jurors a "roadmap of cold, calculated intent" while humanizing each child's interests and focusing on the time and physical effort required to carry out three separate strangulations.

"The prosecution did that because she [Buckingham] wants the jury to remember that the act of strangulation takes time and physical effort," McLean said. "It requires a conscious choice to continue three separate times."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

The Commonwealth’s strategy, she said, is to reject the defense’s bid that Clancy suffered a sudden psychotic break and instead portray her as organized, purposeful and controlled.

During opening statements, defense attorney Kevin Reddington conceded that Clancy killed the children but argued that the only meaningful dispute is what was happening inside her mind.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

"She knows that she killed these children," Reddington told jurors. "The issue for consideration is what was going on in that woman’s mind."

McLean described the concession as a calculated move by a veteran trial attorney.

SEND US A TIP

"By doing that, he is attempting to strip the prosecution of their shock value and force the jury to look purely at Lindsay Clancy’s mental capacity," she said.

Reddington argued that Clancy had no motive to kill children she had loved and nurtured. He also displayed graphic hospital photographs showing Clancy with injuries to her neck and wrists.

GOT A TIP?

McLean said the defense was framing Clancy’s paralysis "not as a consequence of a crime, but as the tragic final symptom of a complete postpartum psychotic break."

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital, has pleaded not guilty to three counts each of murder and strangulation. Her attorneys do not dispute that she killed the children but argue that she lacked criminal responsibility because of severe postpartum psychosis.

Judge William Sullivan told jurors that the Commonwealth must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Clancy was criminally responsible when the children were killed.

"It’s going to be black and white for some people, gray area for other people," McLean said. "It is going to be one of the hardest things that this jury, or any jury, will ever have to decide."

item.title: Heroic 16-year-old lifeguard rescues child from monster surf in heart-stopping video
item.description: Heart-stopping video shows a 16-year-old lifeguard battling relentless waves to save a child from dangerous surf as beachgoers struggled to reach the pair.
item.content:encoded:
A frantic rescue unfolded at a Santa Cruz beach when a child was swept into powerful, tsunami-like waves, prompting a teenage lifeguard to dive into the life-threatening surf.

The lifeguard — whom witnesses said carried out one of the most heroic rescues they had ever seen — was identified as just a 16-year-old high school student, according to local outlet NBC Bay Area. A woman who claimed to be the teenager’s mother said on social media that the lifeguard's name is Ryder.

The young child Ryder rescued is believed to be about 10 years old, according to the report.

Video capturing the terrifying rescue shows multiple beachgoers, along with a second lifeguard, trying to enter the water. Many appeared to be quickly overwhelmed as the massive waves engulfed everyone.

MAN, WOMAN KILLED IN RIP CURRENT AS LIFEGUARD SHORTAGE LEAVES DANGER ZONES IN BEACH DESTINATION

"It caught a lot of people off-guard," Vander Dussen, who filmed the video, said. "Unfortunately, this young man was overwhelmed and swept out in just a moment’s time."

In the video, the 16-year-old lifeguard was seen diving into the water and battling powerful swells to bring the child back to shore.

Wave after wave, Ryder appeared to strategically gulp air before ducking beneath each crashing breaker.

He would then emerge each time still gripping tightly to the child.

As the pair kept getting swallowed by the waves, multiple beachgoers attempted to help, often without success.

‘HERO' MOM DIES AFTER USING LAST STRENGTH TO SAVE 4-YEAR-OLD SON FROM FLORIDA RIVER

The lifeguard ultimately pulled the boy onto shore. According to NBC Bay Area, the child was reunited with his family and was evaluated by paramedics.

Witnesses commenting on the video said the struggle against the waves lasted much longer than the footage shows, adding that Ryder never let go of the child despite the relentless surf.

Ryder's mother, thanking supporters for the outpouring of praise, responded to requests for a GoFundMe page by saying her son was simply doing what he loves.

"I am blown away by the love, kindness, gratitude and respect you're sending his way!" she said.

"A few people have asked about a GoFundMe - but honestly he was just doing the job that he absolutely loves."

Instead, she encouraged those wishing to support Ryder to donate to the Santa Cruz County Parks Department's Junior Guards program, where she said Ryder and many of his fellow lifeguards trained before becoming old enough to serve.

She also argued that lifeguards should be recognized as first responders because of the dangerous surf conditions they face along the Santa Cruz coastline.

Eric Trump also reposted the rescue video with praise.

"Give this 16-year-old lifeguard the highest civilian honor. This is truly the best of America! Well done!," he said.

item.title: California family members claim they were attacked at luxury Maui resort during violent melee
item.description: A California family claims a group hurled chairs and beat relatives as young as 17 at the Kaanapali Alii resort in Lahaina after racial threats.
item.content:encoded:
A California family claims it was targeted in a racially motivated attack at a luxury Maui resort after a group allegedly hurled chairs and beat relatives ranging from teenagers to senior citizens during a chaotic poolside brawl.

Maui police confirmed to Fox News Digital that officers responded to the Kaanapali Alii resort in Lahaina on July 17 around 10 p.m. for a disorderly incident involving approximately 30 people. Police said when officers arrived they found 10 to 15 people still gathered near the pool, several with visible injuries.

Police confirmed the preliminary investigation identified seven California victims between the ages of 17 and 62 who reported that a large group of juveniles assaulted multiple members of their party before fleeing.

According to Maui police, one victim told investigators he and his family were near the pool when an unknown male ran toward them asking for help. Moments later, several juvenile males allegedly chased the individual into the area before turning their attention to others nearby.

CITIES BRACE FOR HOLIDAY WEEKEND TEEN TAKEOVERS PUTTING BYSTANDERS AT DEADLY RISK, FORMER PROSECUTOR WARNS

"The group allegedly began throwing chairs and physically assaulting numerous people in the area, indiscriminately attacking individuals of all ages, including elderly family members who were struck during the incident," Maui police told Fox News Digital.

Family members told Hawaii News Now the alleged attackers repeatedly threatened to "beat up the haole boys" before the violence erupted. 

Merriam-Webster defines "haole" as a Hawaiian term used to describe a foreigner or person of non-Hawaiian descent.

CRAZY BRAWL OVER A PARKING SPOT IN NEW YORK INCLUDES A VICIOUS SKATEBOARD TO THE HEAD

The family told the outlet it wants the assault investigated as a hate crime. Maui police have not classified the incident as a hate crime.

One of the most seriously injured victims was a relative who was struck in the head with a chair while trying to protect family members, suffering a severe head wound that required 13 staples, according to the family.

Police told Fox News Digital that the investigation led to the arrest of a 20-year-old Makawao man on suspicion of second-degree assault. He was later released as the investigation continues. The case is currently classified as an assault/riot, and detectives have interviewed those involved while continuing to gather evidence.

SOCIALIST-LED CALIFORNIA CITY'S CLASH OVER ISRAEL AND ANTISEMITISM OFFERS GLIMPSE INTO THE LEFT'S FUTURE

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Kaanapali Alii said the safety and well-being of its guests, residents and team members "remains our highest priority" and that resort security responded immediately after the violence broke out.

"Upon learning of the altercation, our security team responded promptly, contacted the Maui Police Department and emergency medical services, and remained on scene to assist until first responders arrived," the resort said. "We have provided surveillance footage and are cooperating fully with law enforcement as their investigation continues."

The resort said it is also conducting its own internal review of the incident.

Addressing the family’s allegation that they were targeted because of their race, the resort said it takes claims of racial bias seriously but cautioned against drawing conclusions before detectives complete their investigation.

"We take allegations of this nature seriously," the statement said. "At this time, allegations regarding motive or the circumstances surrounding the incident have not been substantiated, and it would be inappropriate to speculate or draw conclusions while the investigation remains ongoing."

The resort also acknowledged that staff received reports of threats, harassment and disruptive behavior involving individuals connected to the incident before the violence erupted, but declined to discuss those complaints further because of the active criminal investigation.

"Because this remains an active criminal investigation, we cannot comment on specific security actions, witness accounts or other details that could compromise the investigative process," the resort said.

The property said it remains committed to supporting investigators and those affected by the violence.

"Our focus remains on the well-being of our guests, residents and team members, and on assisting law enforcement in every way possible," the statement said.

Anyone with information or video related to the incident is asked to contact the Maui Police Department’s Criminal Investigation Division at (808) 244-6425.

item.title: Fauci's diary shows he fed questions to journalists, built friendships with media figures
item.description: Anthony Fauci's diary entries reveal Jake Tapper texted him questions to ask CNN guests and dined at his home, calling President Donald Trump "totally nuts."
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Anthony Fauci opened up about his relationships with various media personalities in a series of controversial diary entries that put a spotlight on the former White House COVID advisor's cozy relationship with the press. 

Fauci’s diary entries were released on Saturday by Senate Homeland Security Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., detailing the doctor’s role during the COVID-19 crisis through conversations with President Donald Trump, governors, world leaders, media appearances and his personal observations as the pandemic unfolded in 2020. The stunning diary entries reveal that Fauci made fast friends with members of the liberal media who were tasked with covering the pandemic. 

Fauci’s closest media ally appeared to have been CNN anchor Jake Tapper, who was mentioned 41 times in the eyebrow-raising diary. 

ABC, NBC, CBS, CNN AND MS NOW IGNORE FAUCI DIARY ENTRIES THAT REVEAL FIXATION ON FAME DURING COVID

According to the diary, Tapper texted Fauci to mock rival cable news hosts and other doctors. On one occasion, Tapper called to check on Fauci after an appearance on his show irked Trump supporters. 

"Jake wanted to make sure the interview did not cause me any problems," Fauci wrote on April 13, 2020. 

In July 2020, Fauci gushed that he was forming a friendship with Tapper.   

"Had dinner over Jake Tapper and Jen Tapper’s home in DC. Terrific couple. Friendship building," Fauci wrote, according to the diary. 

Later that month, Fauci wrote that he "gave Jake some questions to ask" pediatrician Brett Giroir during an interview on CNN’s "State of the Union." But Tapper would later express frustration, waking Fauci up in the process. 

"Tapper woke me up at 11:23 AM (I went to bed early) furius [sic] at POTUS for tweeting about the fact that Jake severly [sic] questioned Brett Giroir on SOTU CNN show today. Jake was really pissed at the craziness of it all," Fauci wrote. 

The late-night tirade couldn’t have bothered Fauci too much, as he invited Tapper to dinner at his home months later. 

"Had dinner at my home with Jake and Jennifer Tapper. Relaxed, good time. Jake clearly believes that Trump is totally nuts," Fauci wrote on Oct. 23, 2020. 

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

CNN’s Dana Bash sent Fauci a text message in April 2021 after a contentious House Select Subcommittee hearing over COVID-19, according to the diary. The CNN star complimented Fauci and informed the doctor that her CNN colleague also picked a side. 

"Dana Bash sent me a text: ‘I just watched the whole Jordan thing. Again, you’re a better man than I …. As our friend Wolf Blitzer said to me yesterday — no one would have blamed you if you said simply ‘Mr. Jordan, go f--- yourself,’" Fauci wrote. 

Tapper and Bash went on to moderate the CNN Republican Presidential Primary Debate between then-President Biden and President Trump in 2024. 

Meanwhile, Andrea Mitchell celebrated July 4, 2020, by offering a mea culpa to Fauci, who believed the White House was limiting his TV exposure. 

"Andrea Mitchell called my cell very apologetic about not being able to have me on the show since they already booked a couple of governors who were giving exclusives to NBC. I mentioned to her my concern about them keeping me off the air. She was shocked and thought that when I did not come on after requests that it was because I did not want to go on a show," Fauci wrote. 

INSIDE FAUCI'S PRIVATE DIARY: WHAT HE WROTE ABOUT TRUMP, TV PERSONALITIES AND CELEBRITIES

Fauci also had a texting relationship with then-NBC News host Chuck Todd. 

"I had a really nice conversation with Chuck Todd this morning. He had texted me to ask what I thought of the interview yesterday. I told him that I thought it was absolutely terrific, but I wanted some advice from him. I asked him whether he thought that I should pull back from publicly defending myself against the slanderous attacks since that might call more attention to them," Fauci wrote. 

Fauci also revealed that ABC’s George Stephanopoulos texted him following an interview on "Good Morning America" in July 2020. Apparently, Stephanopoulos was impressed that Fauci dismissed a mean tweet from Trump. 

"Thank you, Tony. So impressive," Stephanopoulos wrote, according to the diary. 

Fauci boasted early in the diary that he prepped CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jonathan LaPook for a TV appearance. 

"Also, Jon LaPook was interviewed on CBS Morning News and mentioned me several times since he e-mailed (sic) me over the weekend to prep him for his interview on Universal Flu vaccine and HIV vaccines," Fauci wrote. 

Representatives for NBC News, ABC News and CBS News did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. A spokesperson for CNN declined to comment.

item.title: Brian Harman flips the bird after 3M Open finish, gets a laugh from Scottie Scheffler
item.description: Brian Harman raised his middle finger at a TV camera in the scoring area as Scottie Scheffler erupted in laughter and a fist pump at the 3M Open.
item.content:encoded:
Brian Harman had one final message for a TV camera after the 3M Open, and Scottie Scheffler couldn't stop laughing.

After wrapping up play at TPC Twin Cities in Minnesota, Harman and Scheffler headed to the scoring area to sign their scorecards.

JACKSON KOIVUN HOLDS OFF SCOTTIE SCHEFFLER TO WIN FIRST PGA TOUR EVENT JUST 24 DAYS INTO PRO CAREER

Scheffler had just fired a bogey-free 8-under 63 to finish solo second at 22 under, while Harman posted a final-round 65 to finish tied for third at 20 under.

Both golfers ultimately finished behind 21-year-old Jackson Koivun, who carded a tournament-record 25 under to secure his first PGA Tour victory in just his third start as a professional.

With the round over, the two veterans settled in to sign their scorecards.

A TV camera positioned directly in front of them captured what happened next.

JACKSON KOIVUN ARRIVES IN STYLE, LUCAS GLOVER TAKES OFF HIS SHOES, AND THE GREATEST GOLF DAD MOMENT

Harman looked into the lens and raised his middle finger. Scheffler immediately burst into laughter, punctuating the moment with a fist pump.

JORDAN SPIETH SAYS GAMBLING IS FUELING ROWDY GOLF CROWDS AND WANTS THE SPORT TO ADDRESS IT SOON

The exchange stood out because it unfolded in one of golf's most routine settings, with both players simply signing their scorecards after the round.

The moment caught Scheffler by surprise, with the World No. 1 immediately laughing and pumping his fist after Harman flashed the camera.

It was a brief departure from golf's usual buttoned-up atmosphere and an amusing finish to an otherwise routine afternoon at the 3M Open.

item.title: RFK Jr says Fauci prioritized 'getting on TV' over public health after revealing diary release
item.description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. says Anthony Fauci's diary entries reveal a fixation on fame, claiming the doctor did incalculable damage to public health trust.
item.content:encoded:
Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. condemned Dr. Anthony Fauci on Monday after revealing personal diary entries revealed the doctor’s fixation on fame during the COVID-19 pandemic.

"[Fauci’s] focus was on promoting himself, on getting on TV and not doing public health," Kennedy said on "The Ingraham Angle."

The journals, released by Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., chronicle Fauci's day-to-day life during the COVID-19 pandemic, detailing Fauci’s obsession with his newfound fame and his belief that it was "not hyperbole" to say he was "the most famous and talked about person in the country."

Kennedy, who said he is traumatized by Fauci’s falsehoods, said the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases did "incalculable" damage to public health and dismantled the public’s trust.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

"[Fauci] was the expert that they elevated. And anybody who did not give complete blind faith to these expert opinions – which we now know were lies – was marginalized, vilified, demonized, censored," the HHS secretary told host Laura Ingraham.

Fauci, 85, became largely revered as "America’s doctor" as the public looked to him for guidance during 2020 COVID-19 shutdowns.

ANTHONY FAUCI'S PRIVATE DIARY AND EMAILS SHOW HE KNEW LOCKDOWNS FAILED AND PUSHED MASKS WITHOUT EVIDENCE

RFK Jr. strongly criticized the doctor’s "mismanagement" of the pandemic, emphasizing his role in placing the United States at the highest mortality rate in the world at 3,000 deaths per one million people.

"Because of Dr. Fauci's leadership and other reasons, we had the highest mortality rate from COVID of any country in the world," he told Fox News. "We literally did worse than any nation in the world."

The HHS secretary recalled being de-platformed over questioning Fauci’s assertions about the origins of COVID-19, lamenting how many were "vilified" over spreading "misinformation" that was later deemed to be true.

SLACK MESSAGES RELEASED BY RAND PAUL APPEAR TO SHOW AUTHORS OF KEY COVID-19 ORIGIN PAPER HELD PRIVATE DOUBTS

"I pointed out that [COVID-19] almost certainly came from the Wuhan lab and… my Instagram was canceled with a million followers for misinformation," Kennedy explained. "I never put any misinformation up. I put up all the things that we now know are true and it was called misinformation."

Kennedy pointed fingers at Fauci, saying he is to blame for Americans’ lack of trust in public health and added that "they shouldn’t" because they were "lied to."

He also took aim at legacy media organizations for what he described as suppressing dissenting views and vehemently defending Fauci.

"The press was part of this collaboration," RFK Jr said. "It was corrupt, and it did tremendous damage to the media in this country and to Americans’ faith in that very important democratic institution. It also did incalculable damage to public health."

Kennedy argued Fauci could potentially face perjury prosecution as the doctor faces congressional testimony Wednesday about his diary entries and handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

"There are many things that [Fauci] said that we know are lies, and Rand Paul presumably is going to ask him about those things, and if he lies again, then he could be subject to perjury prosecution," he said.

item.title: Kelsey Grammer admits it's 'exhausting' when movies try to alter history to fit modern tastes
item.description: "Frasier" star Kelsey Grammer told Katie Miller that Hollywood keeps flopping by forcing modern spins on classic stories that ought to respect history and culture.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: "Frasier" star Kelsey Grammer spoke on "The Katie Miller Podcast" about how modern Hollywood keeps getting in its own way.

Podcaster Katie Miller, the wife of White House deputy chief of staff for policy Stephen Miller, observed, "Hollywood seems determined to reinvent nearly every classic, like ‘The Odyssey,’ and distort it just a little bit to fit their views. Have you watched ‘The Odyssey’?"

"I haven't seen ‘The Odyssey,’ so I'm not really too aware of that," Grammer admitted, but added that there are times when certain entertainment "hits me over the head" to the point where, "it's a little exhausting."

He noted that the past was less multicultural than Hollywood would like to portray it, saying, "I think old England is probably full of White people" and that "I think historical significance should be respected a little bit, culturally."

CHRISTOPHER NOLAN CONFIRMS BIZARRE 'THE ODYSSEY' CASTING CHOICES INCLUDING RAPPER TRAVIS SCOTT

"Do you think Hollywood will ever get back there?" Miller asked.

"Yeah. Hollywood isn't very good at telling people what they have to see, you know, because then they flop,’ Grammer replied.

"But they've had, like, successive years of just flops," Miller replied.

One prominent example of a controversial adaptation that flopped was "Snow White," which reportedly netted Disney an approximately $170 million loss. Pixar — under parent company Disney — has tried to pivot away from a series of flops by cutting LGBTQ themes and warning not to make films inspired by the creators' own life stories. 

Pixar Chief Creative Officer Pete Docter told The Wall Street Journal that he chose this pivot because "We’re making a movie, not hundreds of millions of dollars of therapy."

"Yeah. They're probably figuring it out. I think eventually flopping doesn't work so well," Grammer said. "We're not shooting a lot of movies these days. But I mean, I'm glad they made ‘The Odyssey.’ I mean, I don't know if they've, you know, pitched it too far in to our particular culture to divorce you from the idea of what actually happened."

FROM ‘SCREAM’ TO STREAM: JAMIE KENNEDY REVEALS HOW HOLLYWOOD LOST ITS WAY AND WHY HE WON'T GIVE UP ON LA

In recent years, there have been numerous movies in the culture-war spotlight, ranging from remakes like "The Little Mermaid" and "Snow White" to adaptations of ancient history like "Cleopatra" and "The Odyssey." 

Emily Wilson, who famously wrote what some call a feminist translation of Homer’s "The Odyssey" that helped influence the film, panned director Christopher Nolan’s adaptation for missing the spirit of the original heroic epic. The film has also been criticized for using modernized Americanized dialogue, reshaping the character of Odysseus as a more traumatized rather than heroic figure, and for removing many of the mythological aspects.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

In contrast to other controversial adaptations of beloved works, Nolan’s adaptation of "The Odyssey" has managed to become a box office hit, though audiences and critics remain divided over whether its bold creative choices improved the story or missed the mark.

Grammer's full interview with Miller will be published Tuesday night on the show's YouTube page.

item.title: NY Times reporter admits Trump's 'delusional' foes have wrongly written his political obituary many times
item.description: New York Times reporter Jonathan Swan said President Donald Trump showed him a document comparing himself to Napoleon, Stalin, and Genghis Khan in terms of power.
item.content:encoded:
New York Times reporter Jonathan Swan suggested during a "60 Minutes Australia" interview released last week that President Donald Trump has "Napoleonic" ambition and a political survivability that should humble journalists.

Swan and fellow Times reporter Maggie Haberman discussed their new book, "Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump," and Swan offered speculation on the rest of the president's term and cautioned other journalists to have some humility.

"So there's still a sense that, even if Democrats take the House from Trump, they really can't touch him," Swan said in the interview. "And, like you said, his family's made a lot of money. He's wealthier than he's ever been. He has immunity conferred by the Supreme Court. And there's no prospect, even if he does get impeached, there's no prospect of a conviction."

"I think Donald Trump's obituary has been written so many times — his political obituary — by so many people," Swan continued. "And by this point, if you don't have some humility around that, I think, you know, you're operating in a fairly delusional way. This is someone who has incredible survival capacities, who's able to regenerate himself, and he's still got two and a half years left as the most powerful man on the planet, with no intention of receding at all."

HOW TRUMP SURVIVES: BATTLING THE MEDIA, FORMER ALLIES AND ASSASSINATION ATTEMPTS

As he spoke about the future of Trump’s term, he noted that the president's next step may be taking on the Cuban regime. 

"So there are many things he could do," he said. "The most obvious in foreign policy is Cuba. They've been looking at potential regime change in Cuba, but who knows? It's a big world out there, and we don't want to start being pundits and prognosticating."

Swan also described a past encounter at the White House that he suggested speaks volumes about Trump’s personal mindset and policies. As Trump met with Swan and Haberman, he had purportedly shown them a document he claimed was written by a historian.

"So it opens by saying Donald Trump is the most powerful man who's ever existed, ever lived on the planet, by far," Swan said. "And then it goes on to compare him to what Donald Trump said was, to us, the top ten. And it was Stalin, Mao, Hitler, Napoleon, Attila the Hun, Genghis Khan, the Caesars, Alexander the Great, Tamerlane ... there's probably one I'm missing."

TRUMP AIMS TO RESET WAR POWERS CLOCK WITH CONTROVERSIAL BID TO BYPASS CONGRESS

"And it had nothing to do with morality," Swan continued. "The document didn't mention morality. It was about power and raw power."

The premise of the document, Swan said, was that Trump is the most powerful leader in history and is willing to use power in a way no previous president has done within their lifetime, which he noted was remarkably similar to the book he wrote about the administration.

Swan added further, "I think it's also that he wants to be a sort of Napoleonic ... you know, the person who only needs to be known by one name, who is the defining figure of our age. And so, when Trump thinks about himself in history, I don't think he's comparing himself to Bill Clinton or, you know, name your U.S. president — Eisenhower. I think it is to figures like Napoleon and that he wants to be the defining global figure of our age."

In response to Swan's comments, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told Fox News Digital that "President Trump is fighting every day to deliver the strong, safe, and prosperous country that we all deserve. The only legacy President Trump is concerned with is making America greater than ever before."

item.title: White House fires back after John Mellencamp mocks Trump's Gulf of America during concert
item.description: John Mellencamp paused his "Pink Houses" performance to mock Trump's Gulf of America executive order, prompting a sharp White House response.
item.content:encoded:
The White House is hitting back after John Mellencamp took direct shots at President Donald Trump's Gulf of America.

Mellencamp paused his Saturday night show Holmdel, N.J. to mock Trump's executive order to rename the "Gulf of Mexico" to "Gulf of America."

On Monday, Davis Ingle, WH Spokesman, shared a statement with Fox News Digital. "Nobody in their right mind cares what out-of-touch, woke Hollywood celebrities have to say," Ingle said.

As part of his "Dancing Words" Tour, Mellencamp was singing the first few verses of his hit "Pink Houses," before he addressed the crowd directly.

WHITE HOUSE FIRES BACK AFTER ROBERT DE NIRO, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN TAKE TRUMP SWIPES AMID COLBERT'S FAREWELL WEEK

"Well, there’s people and more people/ What do they know, know, know?/ Go to work in some high rise/ And vacation down at the Gulf of Mexico," the rock icon sang before adding, "Wait a minute," according to USA Today.

While Mellencamp's band kept playing, the musician said sarcastically, "The Gulf of Mexico? Is that right? It’s not the Gulf of America? What a stupid f–----g idea."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Mellencamp then picked right back up and finished performing "Pink Houses."

Released in 1983, Mellencamp's "Pink Houses" became one of his signature hits, reaching No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100.

While many listeners initially embraced it as a patriotic anthem, Mellencamp has said the song is actually a sharp commentary on the American dream, exploring themes of class, inequality and the gap between ideals and reality.

The song was inspired by Mellencamp spotting a man sitting outside a small pink house along an Indiana highway, an image that sparked the iconic chorus, "Ain't that America."

item.title: Trump's $15B lawsuit against The New York Times carries on as judge gives his attorneys chance to amend filing
item.description: President Trump celebrates after a judge allows his legal team to amend the massive $15 billion defamation lawsuit against The New York Times by August 27.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump took a victory lap Monday after a judge granted his legal team a chance to amend his $15 billion defamation lawsuit against The New York Times.

"BREAKING NEWS: The Failing New York Times, after 10 years of harassment, slander, and libel, just failed again in their desperate attempt to have our powerful Defamation Lawsuit against them dropped," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "As we requested, the Highly Respected Judge has called for an updated complaint, which will lay out, in extreme detail, all the ways in which The Times has repeatedly and consistently acted, with actual malice in defaming me, my family, our Great MAGA Movement, and America, itself."

"We will continue to hold The Times and their 'comrades' in the Mainstream Media accountable for publishing, promoting, and dealing in Fake News. Thank you for your attention to this matter!" Trump added.

TRUMP THREATENS TO ADD NY TIMES' 'TREASONOUS' IRAN WAR COVERAGE TO $15B DEFAMATION LAWSUIT

According to a filing in the U.S. District Court for Florida’s Middle District in Tampa, Trump's attorneys have until August 27 to amend the lawsuit.

The New York Times did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

The suit alleged decades of defamation and libel by the Times over everything from how it reported on "The Apprentice" to its stories claiming he'd engaged in suspect tax maneuvers.

TRUMP DOJ WITHDRAWS SUBPOENAS TARGETING NEW YORK TIMES JOURNALISTS AMID LEAK PROBE

The named defendants are The New York Times Company, reporters Susanne Craig, Russ Buettner, Peter Baker and Michael S. Schmidt, and Penguin Random House, which published "Lucky Loser: How Donald Trump Squandered His Father’s Fortune and Created the Illusion of Success," which was authored by Craig and Buettner.

A spokesperson for The Times previously told Fox News Digital, "As we said when this was first filed and again after the judge’s ruling to strike it: this lawsuit has no merit. Nothing has changed today. This is merely an attempt to stifle independent reporting and generate PR attention, but The New York Times will not be deterred by intimidation tactics."

item.title: 19 cadets rushed to hospitals after mystery illness strikes military-style youth academy in DC area
item.description: A mass casualty response was launched at a Maryland National Guard youth academy after cadets reported dizziness, headaches and nausea on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
At least 19 cadets at a military-style youth academy in the Washington, D.C., area were sent to area hospitals Sunday after reporting symptoms of an unknown illness, prompting a mass casualty response, officials said.

Emergency crews responded to the Capital Guardian Youth Challenge Academy in Laurel, Maryland, after cadets began experiencing symptoms following lunch, the DC National Guard said, according to FOX 5 DC.

The academy, which is operated by the DC National Guard, is a military-style life intervention program for at-risk teens, according to the institution.

CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK: IS IT STILL SAFE TO EAT AT RESTAURANTS? HERE'S WHAT TO KNOW

One mother told FOX 5 that blood tests at a hospital showed her son had elevated carbon monoxide levels. He reportedly developed delayed symptoms hours after other cadets were taken for treatment, including dizziness, headaches and nausea.

The mother added that the youth academy decided to temporarily close following the incident.

However, Anne Arundel County Fire Department officials said they conducted a carbon monoxide investigation and did not detect elevated levels of the gas, according to the local station.

DOCTORS WARN YOUR 'STOMACH BUG' MAY ACTUALLY BE A PARASITE THAT'S HARDER TO DETECT

Officials have not confirmed the cause of the illness but said it could be related to food.

DC National Guard officials said the health and safety of cadets and staff remain their highest priority and that they are working with emergency medical personnel and public health authorities as the investigation continues, according to FOX 5.

Officials added that while 19 cadets were sent to area hospitals, one adult was evaluated at the scene and declined further medical treatment.

Fox News Digital reached out to D.C. National Guard for more information.

item.title: 'Baywatch' star Brooks Nader suffers wardrobe malfunction during Saint-Tropez getaway

item.content:encoded:

Between filming Fox's upcoming "Baywatch" reboot in Los Angeles and hopping from one European hotspot to another, the 29-year-old model has kept fans updated every step of the way.

BROOKS NADER NARROWLY AVOIDS WARDROBE MALFUNCTION MINUTES BEFORE 'BAYWATCH' REBOOT RED CARPET

Nader gave followers a behind-the-scenes look aboard a luxury yacht through a series of Instagram Stories, including one that showed her posing in the same leopard-print halterneck playsuit after sunset.

A change of scenery also meant a change of outfit.

In another Instagram Story, Nader traded the leopard-print ensemble for a casual white two-piece while walking barefoot up an elegant wooden staircase. She paired a fitted white tank top with cheeky white shorts that read "Saint-Tropez French Riviera" across the back.

BROOKS NADER WOWS IN ICONIC RED ONE-PIECE BATHING SUIT AS 'BAYWATCH' REBOOT FILMS BEACH SCENES

Sharing another Story as she departed the yacht, Nader filmed her friends waving goodbye before writing, "Torture leaving my fave place & peeps, back to work I go."

BROOKS NADER FLAUNTS HER TONED ABS IN BLACK BIKINI WHILE FILMING HER REALITY SHOW

The insider added that Nader is currently balancing production on Fox's upcoming "Baywatch" reboot alongside filming the second season of her Hulu and Freeform reality series, "Love Thy Nader."

Nader also recently dismissed romance rumors herself, telling TMZ she and Egerton "never were" dating and insisting she's "just single, having fun, always."

Before that, the model dated her former "Dancing with the Stars" partner Gleb Savchenko following the end of her marriage to advertising executive Billy Haire. She has also been linked to tennis stars Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner.

item.title: Pro Bowl player requests trade from Tampa Bay Buccaneers on eve of training camp amid contract dispute
item.description: Vita Vea's trade request comes as the Pro Bowl nose tackle ranks 19th in pay among interior linemen despite anchoring Tampa Bay's top-ranked run defense.
item.content:encoded:
As negotiation tactics go, asking for a trade the day before training camp opens is the NFL equivalent of reaching for the nuclear codes before deciding to type them in. But that's exactly what Tampa Bay Buccaneers nose tackle Vita Vea has done.

The two-time Pro Bowl player has grown so frustrated with contract discussions this offseason that he's decided he doesn't see a future with the team, and has asked to be traded, a league source confirmed to Fox News Digital.

That doesn't mean a trade will happen. Vea is under contract for the 2026 season and is scheduled to make up to $18 million if he can play all 17 games in the final year of his current contract.

A.J. BROWN HEADED TO NEW ENGLAND TO REUNITE WITH MIKE VRABEL AFTER A SEASON OF EAGLES UNHAPPINESS

The Bucs aren't simply going to hold a fire sale to avoid the trade talk distraction, per a source.

Vea wants more money and points to the fact he is currently the 19th-highest-paid interior defensive lineman in the league. And he believes he is much better than the 19th-best defensive lineman in the league.

Vea is, for all intents and purposes, the structural centerpiece of the Tampa Bay defense. He is arguably the team's best run defender and, as all NFL defensive coordinators often note, if a defense cannot stop the run it is unable to do much of anything else.

Vea provides a rare combination of size, power to movement to control the middle of the formation from his nose tackle spot. At 6-foot-4 and 347 pounds, Vea has anchored against double-teams for much of his recent years.

Despite this attention, he is able to clog interior rushing lanes and prevent offensive linemen from climbing cleanly to the second level of Tampa Bay’s defense. Since becoming a full-time starter in 2019, he has helped the Buccaneers establish one of the NFL’s most consistently productive run defenses.

From 2019 through most of the 2024 season, Tampa Bay ranked first in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game at 94.1, first in yards allowed per carry at 4.0 and finished in the top five against the run in five of six seasons, including No. 1 finishes in 2019 and 2020.

COWBOYS LOCK IN GEORGE PICKENS WITH $27.3M FRANCHISE TAG DESPITE FAILING TO REACH LONG-TERM CONTRACT

Vea played only five games in 2020 due to a fractured ankle, but he's proven durable ever since. He has started 78 games in the past five seasons.

Vea’s individual production shows he is more than a traditional space-eating nose tackle but he set a career high with seven sacks in 2024, then added 4.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss and 13 quarterback hits in 2025.

His 2024 pass-rush production made Tampa Bay one of only three teams that season with two defensive tackles recording at least seven sacks, as Vea and Calijah Kancey both reached that mark.

Vea was selected to the Pro Bowl following the 2021 and 2024 seasons, earned a place on the NFL Players Association’s Top 100 list entering 2025 and was a key member of Tampa Bay’s Super Bowl LV championship team.

This trade request creates issues for the Bucs.

It's possible Vea, who reported but did not take part in the teams mandatory minicamp and missed the rest of the offseason program, might decide to simply hold in to start training camp – that is to say, he shows up but doesn't practice.

No coach likes that. No team wants that.

The Buccaneers are already managing the high-stakes contract negotiations with quarterback Baker Mayfield as their top contract issue. So dealing with a very large star defender who has publicly let it be known he wants out is not great for the team.

item.title: WNBA love feud explodes as NaLyssa Smith fires back at DiJonai Carrington's cheating claims
item.description: NaLyssa Smith went live on Twitch to address DiJonai Carrington's cheating allegations, questioning why the Chicago Sky guard aired their breakup publicly.
item.content:encoded:
Las Vegas Aces forward NaLyssa Smith went live on Twitch to respond after ex-girlfriend DiJonai Carrington accused her of a multi-player cheating scandal.

During a livestream, Smith refused to confirm or deny the allegations, instead questioning why the Chicago Sky guard chose to air their private history a year after their breakup.

Carrington launched the feud on Threads by alleging Smith cheated on her with Aces teammate Deja Kelly, Atlanta Dream guard Aaliyah Nye and others.

WNBA ROCKED BY MULTI-PLAYER CHEATING SCANDAL AS DIJONAI CARRINGTON CALLS OUT EX NALYSSA SMITH

"Whether she cheated on me and I cheated on her, why are we bringing that to the internet a year later when nobody did anything to anybody? Whether she cheated on me or I cheated on her, that has nothing to do with anybody," Smith said. "Like what? That don't even make sense. And to bring it to the internet a year later, is crazy. Just for fun? That's ridiculous, especially when you're in a happy, healthy relationship."

Smith also criticized Carrington for dragging Kelly and Nye into the public dispute.

WNBPA SAYS IT DID NOT ASK WNBA TO DROP USA 250 ALL-STAR PATCH AFTER UNION OFFICER PUBLICLY OBJECTED

"Then, to bring up folks name that has nothing to do with anything. These folks is minding their business. These folks woke up to this s**t on a random Sunday night of these type of allegations," Smith said. "I think that's very weird."

Detailing the in-person confrontation that preceded Carrington's social media outburst, Smith claimed Carrington started an argument that ended with security stepping in.

"Here goes DiJonai. 'You talkin to that b*tch. You talkin to that b*tch.' B*tch this. B*tch that. I'm like 'Why I gotta be a b*tch?' Literally on my grandmother's grave, I'm like 'Damn why I gotta be a b*tch.' That's how the whole thing started," Smith said. "I'm literally like 'Who's a b*tch?' So, then it causes commotion and I'm just like 'Damn now what?' I look like the problem. So, then security come and he's like 'Alright y'all gonna have to leave.' Mind y'all, I'm the victim."

Smith also denied online claims that she showed up uninvited to keep tabs on Carrington.

WNBA COMMISSIONER VOWS TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RACISM, MISOGYNY,' DODGES BIG QUESTIONS AT ALL-STAR PRESS CONFERENCE

"I didn't do 'none.' I'm sitting on the couch posting, minding my business. I didn't do nothing to nobody," Smith said. "So, the fact that people are trying to create this narrative of 'Lyss came somewhere uninvited and she came here just to spy on folks. Y'all gotta stop all that lying."

Smith suggested alcohol contributed to Carrington's outburst.

"I guess the liquor, the cameras, her crowd, I guess she got some type of, somebody boosted her up to gain some confidence," Smith said. "But at the end of the day, that was some bulls–t. We came to the spot. Folks was chilling. Nobody did nothing to nobody."

The former Baylor teammates will meet on the court Aug. 1, when Carrington's Sky host Smith and the Aces in Chicago.

item.title: Netflix exec claims ketamine confession in ‘trust exercise’ cost him $1.1M job: lawsuit
item.description: Kevin Baillie says he shared his medically supervised ketamine therapy for depression during a vulnerability exercise at a Netflix workplace retreat.
item.content:encoded:
Former Netflix executive Kevin Baillie has sued the streaming giant, according to court papers reported by The New York Post Sunday, after he said he was fired in April from its Eyeline Studios division because he disclosed medically supervised ketamine treatment for depression during a workplace retreat.

"The ketamine therapy issue has factored into the termination," the attorney said, according to the lawsuit.

Baillie, who served as vice president and head of creative at the visual effects division, earned about $1.1 million annually. The complaint said Netflix also denied him as much as one year of severance pay following his dismissal stemming from his comments in January at Netlix-owned Sendero Ranch in Northern California, according to the suit.

He said he underwent ketamine therapy at a Santa Barbara clinic in 2022 while experiencing clinical depression following his mother's death. He said the drug was prescribed and administered under medical supervision, according to the report.

TRUMP SIGNS EXECUTIVE ORDER DIRECTING FDA TO REVIEW PSYCHEDELICS DESIGNATED AS BREAKTHROUGH THERAPY DRUGS

The executive disclosed the treatment during a vulnerability-trust exercise that encouraged employees to share personal experiences. When a Netflix investigator questioned him March 18, the complaint said the therapy was presented as potential recreational drug use.

The investigator raised the treatment "in a manner suggesting suspicion of recreational drug use," the complaint said, according to the Post.

Baillie said the company’s investigation also examined allegations that he used profanity and consumed alcohol. His previous performance review had addressed his language but did not direct him to stop swearing entirely.

"Drop one or two less f-bombs but don’t stop entirely," the performance review said, according to the complaint.

VALERIE BERTINELLI APOLOGIZES AFTER DROPPING F-BOMB ON LIVE TV

The lawsuit said Baillie also told colleagues during the retreat that his former father-in-law had taught him to drink a Guinness while standing on his head. A colleague then asked Baillie to demonstrate the trick.

"His colleague immediately asked for a demonstration," the complaint said. "Rather than withhold the openness that the session had encouraged, he performed the trick."

Netflix’s public culture memo promotes vulnerability and candor while describing the company as a professional sports team rather than a family. Managers apply a "keeper test" when deciding whether to retain employees, although the memo also said workers should receive regular feedback and be evaluated on their entire record.

"If the answer is no, we believe it’s fairer to everyone to part ways quickly," Netflix said of the "keeper test," which entails candidly assessing if one would fight to keep a worker if they wanted to leave, or if they would hire the person again if they knew everything they do now.

"You willingly receive and give feedback; you are open about what’s working and what needs to improve; you admit mistakes openly and share learnings widely," the site states.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Ketamine is a Schedule III controlled substance that is federally approved as an anesthetic and is also prescribed off-label for depression. The FDA has separately approved the ketamine-derived nasal spray Spravato for treatment-resistant depression under medical supervision.

Baillie is seeking a jury trial, lost wages, compensatory and punitive damages and damages for emotional distress. He previously worked on visual effects for the "Pirates of the Caribbean" and "Harry Potter" franchises. 

Netflix had not publicly responded to his allegations as of Monday. Fox News Digital reached out to Baillie and Netflix for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Biden's classified docs narrative crumbles amid release of ghostwriter tapes: 'Be careful'
item.description: Over 2.5 hours of recordings between Joe Biden and memoir ghostwriter Mark Zwonitzer reveal halting speech and memory struggles during the 2017 sessions.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden's recordings from interviews with his memoir ghostwriter — obtained during special counsel Robert Hur's classified documents investigation — have been released to the public.

After a months-long fight from Biden’s attorneys to block the release of the tape, they abandoned their lawsuit calling for a dismissal Friday, in which a judge accepted Monday.

The plaintiff, Mike Howell formerly with conservative think tank Heritage Foundation and now at Oversight Project, has fought for more than two years to obtain the materials through FOIA requests, arguing that the public has an interest in reviewing the recordings and transcripts on which Hur based his decision.

BIDEN'S HUR INTERVIEW TAPES COULD NOW GO PUBLIC AFTER HIS ATTORNEYS WAVE WHITE FLAG

The Oversight Project published hours of recordings from Biden's 2016 and 2017 conversations with his "Promise Me, Dad" ghostwriter, Mark Zwonitzer, in which the then-former vice president frequently pauses, speaks haltingly and struggles to recall events — reinforcing Special Counsel Robert Hur's characterization in his report.

"Joe Biden didn’t want these tapes to come out. But now they have — after two years of painful delay. There is no joy in Bidenville today. Robert Hur’s and Merrick Garland’s decision to give Biden a free pass for keeping and disclosing classified information must now be reexamined from top to bottom," Oversight Project Vice President of Litigation Jeff Clark exclusively told Fox News Digital.

The House Judiciary Committee announced there were 2 hours and 45 minutes of recordings released. 

Hur investigated Biden’s handling of classified documents dating from his time as vice president in the Obama administration and as a U.S. senator from Delaware. He declined to pursue criminal charges because he concluded prosecutors could not prove beyond a reasonable doubt that Biden willfully retained or disclosed the material.

HUNTER BIDEN RESURFACES IN LA, REACTS TO QUESTIONS ABOUT BIDEN TAPES, UFO FILES

In his report, Hur wrote that Biden’s conversations were "painfully slow" and said Biden was "struggling to remember events and straining at times to read and relay his own notebook entries."

"Mr. Biden's memory was significantly limited, both during his recorded interviews with the ghostwriter in 2017 and in his interview with our office in 2023," wrote Hur.

He also said, in shocking reasoning for the lack of prosecution, that Biden could appear to a jury as a "sympathetic, well-meaning, elderly man with a poor memory" rather than an intentional violator of classified document laws.

The interview recordings show instances where Biden takes long pauses, forgets names, and can't recall specific days. 

Biden warned Zwonitzer while discussing a 2014 Situation Room meeting, "Some of this may be classified, so be careful," and added, "I'm not sure. It isn't marked classified, but...."

In one instance, on April 24, 2017, Biden struggled to recall two economic advisers.

 "I’ll think of his name," said Biden, and then, "I should write the names down because I keep forgetting them." A long pause follows before Zwonitzer says Alan Krueger’s name.

On the same day, Biden fails to recall where he was on a certain date, later remembering he was at a memorial for a fallen service member – and forgot his name.

"I think I went to that memorial service in Wilmington. It says [REDACTED] December the 4th, but I don't -- I know what this means. Memorial service -- [REDACTED] gets names really f---ed up," said Biden. "So it says memorial service for [REDACTED]. I don't think her name was [REDACTED]. Or I forget [REDACTED]."

Zwonitzer responded, "Okay," and Biden said he would "make a note of that too."

"But at any rate, back to -- there was -- I had a meeting with Ron Klain, and I don't know when," Biden added. 

Biden also appeared to struggle in recalling a lunch with former United States Secretary of the Treasury Larry Summers.

"When he, when he came to me — and I’ll get the date. Remind me when did Summers come to me to have lunch to — it was when I was thinking about running."

He later goes on to say, "Here’s what happened, before I forget. Don’t mind my train of thought. He also pledged to support me in 2016."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Office of Joe Biden for comment.

item.title: Fishing content creator who filmed himself being bitten by a shark while spearfishing lucky he still has leg
item.description: Footage shows the grey reef shark circling before biting Henry Gibbs' leg during a spearfishing dive in Fiji, requiring four surgeries and a skin graft.
item.content:encoded:
A fishing content creator from New Zealand is lucky to still have his leg after going for a dive in Fiji. Henry Gibbs was spearfishing earlier this month in the water near the South Pacific island when he was bitten by a grey reef shark.

The damage from the bite to his right leg required four surgeries and a skin graft, but didn’t cause him to lose any ability to use his foot.

"No hard feelings towards the shark. I was in its environment hunting its food," Gibbs wrote in an Instagram post a few days ago that included pictures of him in a hospital bed.

"Wrong place, wrong time, and there are definitely a few lessons I'll share when I post the footage in the hope it helps someone avoid ending up in the same situation and a bit on how to respond to it."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

On Sunday, the fishing influencer followed through on that and shared the footage of the shark circling below before racing toward him and taking a bite out of his lower leg.

Gibbs explained that they had been diving in the reef for an hour or two before making their way to clearer blue water. They were trying to do some spearfishing and had a "handful of grey reef sharks" hanging out near them.

One of the sharks in particular hung around longer than the others. He doesn’t know if it was the commotion coming from the boat, the speargun sounds or the general activity in the water that made the shark excited.

'SHARK WEEK' HOST FORREST GALANTE EXPLAINS WHY CRUSHING BEERS IN THE OCEAN IS A BAD IDEA

"I'll never know exactly what caused the change, but eventually it started making tight semicircles beneath us, became increasingly agitated and even sprinted at the boat," Gibbs wrote in the caption of the shark attack footage.

"Looking back, that should've been enough of a sign to call the dive. I never thought a shark of that size posed much of a threat, and that was a mistake."

He added that most of his encounters with sharks have come in New Zealand, where he says the sharks are less aggressive. A big mistake on his part was expecting this shark to act in the same manner.

Having been bitten by a shark, Gibbs has some takeaways he'd like to pass along. The first is to end the dive and move on if a shark's behavior changes. He also suggests sticking to plain black wetsuits in the tropics.

He's heard of several incidents now that he's been attacked of grey reef sharks going after divers in camouflage wetsuits. His last two takeaways are to not ignore an agitated shark and to not judge the risk by the shark's size.

Gibbs teased that there's more footage that's more graphic than what he already shared. He also thanked those who reached out and who have cared for him since the bite.

"I'm still deciding whether to share the rest of the footage as it becomes very graphic, but I do want to share more about carrying proper trauma gear, knowing how to use it, and diving with people you trust," he wrote.

"A huge thank you to everyone who's reached out, and to all the doctors, nurses and hospital staff, family and friends who've looked after me."

You can add spearfishing in Fiji near grey reef sharks to the list of activities you're not going to find me attempting.

item.title: Store clerk foiled ex-Navy SEAL's explosives plot targeting police at No Kings protest, feds say
item.description: A store clerk's tip led federal agents to Gregory Vandenberg after he allegedly revealed his plan to hurl explosives at law enforcement during protests.
item.content:encoded:
A former U.S. Navy SEAL was convicted in a foiled plot to attack law enforcement officers with explosives during a "No Kings" protest in California after a store clerk's tip led federal investigators to him.

Gregory Vandenberg, 49, was found guilty after a five-day federal trial of transportation of explosives with intent to kill, injure or intimidate and attempted transportation of prohibited fireworks into California, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of New Mexico.

Jurors deliberated for about three hours before returning the guilty verdict.

Prosecutors said Vandenberg was driving from El Paso, Texas, to San Diego ahead of the June 14, 2025, demonstrations when he stopped at a travel center near Lordsburg, New Mexico, and purchased six mortar-style fireworks and 72 M-150 firecrackers.

FORMER MARINE GETS 100 YEARS IN PRISON AS JUDGE CALLS ICE DETENTION CENTER AMBUSH 'AN ASSAULT ON DEMOCRACY'

While making the purchase, Vandenberg told a store clerk he intended to throw the explosives at law enforcement officers during the protests, federal authorities said.

He repeatedly asked about the amount of gunpowder in the fireworks, whether taping multiple mortars together would increase their explosive force and said he was interested only in their ability to injure officers, prosecutors said.

'SOMETHING BIG': FEDS REVEAL HOW RELATIVES OF SUSPECTS IN FOILED WHITE HOUSE UFC PLOT SAW WARNING SIGNS

Vandenberg also encouraged the clerk to attend the protests and hand out fireworks to others, telling the employee he would not get hurt because of his military experience, according to trial testimony.

The conversation alarmed employees enough that they wrote down Vandenberg's license plate and contacted law enforcement before he reached California.

Federal agents tracked Vandenberg to Davis-Monthan Air Force Base in Tucson, Arizona, where he was arrested the following morning while sleeping inside his vehicle.

ANTI-ISRAEL DEMONSTRATOR SENTENCED TO YEAR IN JAIL FOR MANSLAUGHTER DURING 2023 PROTESTS

Prosecutors said he falsely claimed he was traveling for work despite being unemployed and later told investigators he was visiting friends in Phoenix.

A search of Vandenberg's vehicle uncovered the fireworks along with clothing displaying antisemitic, anti-Israel and extremist imagery, according to prosecutors.

Among the items recovered were shirts bearing an Al-Qaeda flag, a shirt calling for the destruction of Judea, a hat featuring the Al-Qaeda flag and apparel displaying a variation of the Black Sun, a symbol associated with neo-Nazi ideology.

Jurors were also shown photographs of Vandenberg wearing a custom-made T-shirt bearing the word "AMALEK" while inside the travel center. Prosecutors said Vandenberg told investigators the word meant "destroyer of Jews."

Investigators also discovered Vandenberg's cellphone home screen displayed a Taliban flag. A forensic review of the phone uncovered what prosecutors described as violent extremist content, including antisemitic, anti-Israel and anti-U.S. material, as well as messages discussing the upcoming protests.

According to prosecutors, those messages suggested Vandenberg believed the U.S. government, including President Donald Trump, was controlled by Israel and Jewish people, evidence they argued helped establish his motive for targeting law enforcement officers.

"People in this country are free to hold their own beliefs and to express them peacefully," Acting U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison said in a statement. "What they are not free to do is use explosives to threaten or terrorize others."

Ellison added that Vandenberg "intended to turn explosives into a tool of intimidation," and said the verdict "sends the message that attempts to substitute violence for expressing one's opinion has no place in our communities and will be met with federal consequences."

Vandenberg was later sentenced to 16 months in federal prison, where he remains in custody. Upon his release, he will serve one year of supervised release.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan 'this close' to losing his right eye in horrible car crash, NFL analyst reveals
item.description: NFL analyst Chris Simms said Kyle Shanahan nearly lost his right eye in the July 14 car crash after viewing jarring photos from the coach's wife.
item.content:encoded:
Former NFL quarterback Chris Simms revealed that his close friend, San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan, almost lost an eye during a horrible car crash he was involved in earlier this month.

Simms, who is a current NFL analyst, made an appearance on "PFT Live" where he explained pictures he received from Shanahan’s wife, Mandy, after the July 14 accident occurred.

"When you first see it, and it’s fresh, and some of the cuts are still wide open, I mean, it’s jarring," Simms explained. "It’s jarring.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"He was this close to maybe losing his right eye."

The injuries were quite significant for Shanahan, who is limited to starting training camp with the 49ers, the team announced.

Shanahan suffered a broken nose, three broken ribs and a broken hand. He also needed over 40 stitches in his face and had a severe concussion after colliding with another SUV by his home in Northern California, per ESPN.

ROGER GOODELL DISMISSES 49ERS COACH'S CONCERNS ABOUT PLAYING IN AUSTRALIA, SAYS IT'S PART OF LONG-TERM PLAN

"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week when he suffered non-life threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers," the team said in its statement.

"Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care."

Simms pointed to his forehead when he said, "The scar is so big right here."

"So, all that stuff was just crazy to see," he added.

While Shanahan has yet to speak on the crash, Simms did reveal some of what he is feeling at the moment.

"He was emotional about it because he realized how close it was to being just a complete, you know, utter disaster," Simms, who mentioned the other driver was a woman, said. "Like, really, it was a disaster anyways. But, when you’re a part of that accident, like I said, he could have lost his right eye. It could have been a lot worse. You know, he’s very concerned about the woman he got in the accident with and how she is and handling that situation. So there’s just a lot there. And I think it was a lot for him to process."

Shanahan was spotted at 49ers training camp on Sunday, where his face was masked by a baseball hat and sunglasses.

GM John Lynch also noted that, "Kyle basically is going to be like in the protocol," in reference to his concussion. Simms said it is giving him "some issues" he must deal with through the healing process.

While Shanahan serves his team on a limited basis, Chris Foerster, the 49ers’ assistant head coach, is acting in his place.

The 49ers open the season against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10 in the first-ever game played in Australia.
